nodes.title: Palimpsest
nodes.why: F4, visibility and the vanishing record
nodes.curated_why: The most sourced room (eleven symbols, raking light, the Archimedes leaf) and the source of the sound-to-liquid seam through its signal motif.

nodes.title: The False Balance
nodes.curated_why: The False Balance is the anchor set piece of the false-scale family: concrete beam, iron wedge, eleven sourced symbols, and the mirror line pointed at our own pan.

nodes.title: Powers of Ten, for a Lie
nodes.curated_why: Powers of Ten, for a Lie uses the same zoom the universe uses, so the map's own motion has a room that explains it; it shares the Eames reference with We Are Here.

nodes.title: The test that wasn't
nodes.curated_why: The test that wasn't: the planted pass told as a room, and Flywheel's dual-edge twin, so the first drift from the grid lands on its own shadow.

nodes.title: Four labels
nodes.curated_why: Four labels is the label-that-moves family in one image, built from cleared 1918 front pages and screen-print halftone, and Articulate's twin.

nodes.title: Manufactured consensus
nodes.curated_why: Manufactured consensus: one signal split into many traces, the clearest dot-field piece, and the room Daylight's coordination lens answers.

nodes.title: Flywheel
nodes.blurb: Flywheel runs AI tasks with the model you choose and checks each answer against the task contract. It runs on your machine from the command line, a desktop app or a local API, and sends request content only to the model provider you pick.
nodes.curated_why: The flagship and the instrument the whole site is built around; its page is the CS-max direction made real, and its counts feed the data-to-brush seam.

nodes.title: Articulate
nodes.blurb: Articulate is prose analysis and model-assisted editing for the command line, editors and CI. It names each writing pattern it finds and the line it is on, in the terminal, in an editor through its language server, or as SARIF in code review.

nodes.title: Daylight Commons
nodes.why: Reads feeds for coordination and drift (MAP F5 and F2).

nodes.title: BuildLang
nodes.blurb: BuildLang is a systems programming language in which a program declares what it is allowed to touch. The compiler checks those declarations and its memory rules, then emits native code through C. It ships with a CLI, editor support, two-way C integration and experimental shader output.

nodes.title: EMET
nodes.blurb: EMET checks whether the bytes that reach a model, reviewer or pipeline still match their source. It anchors content, compares it later, neutralizes instructions embedded in it, and writes a verdict file that its Python, Rust, Node and Go implementations all read the same way.

nodes.title: raw-native
nodes.blurb: RAW is a dependency-free C++23 renderer that draws a scene on the CPU, checks its fast screen-space ambient occlusion against a ray-traced reference, and writes a JSON certificate saying whether the shortcut held.
nodes.why: raw is béton brut's own word; the renderer shows the fast frame beside the reference.

nodes.title: Engine Revival
nodes.blurb: Engine Revival is a Python tool for building, checking and publishing metadata about revived historical engines. It can also generate an out-of-tree BRender CMake build harness from a public checkout.

nodes.title: Low Water
nodes.why: Each trait embodied and fought: the inner arena.

nodes.title: learn
nodes.blurb: Learn plans study sessions from your objectives and recorded attempts, using spaced review, retrieval practice, prerequisite checks and misconception tracking. It can also handle course logistics and stops at graded work.
nodes.why: The learning platform sits with the deco orrery of guides.

nodes.title: BRender archival
nodes.blurb: BRender Archival rebuilds the Argonaut BRender engine from its public MIT source, runs it through a 21-stage native test ladder, captures renders, and packages the build harness, test transcripts and checksums without copying the upstream source.
nodes.why: An archived engine kept and rebuilt.

nodes.title: Gallery
nodes.blurb: Name a seed, pick from ninety-five instruments, and this site's own engine draws your plate in the browser. Forty-two full-size plates sit below it.

nodes.title: Studio
nodes.blurb: A live media instrument for rendering, measuring, transforming, and reading the frame, running entirely in your own browser.
nodes.why: Generative work in cells and traces.

nodes.title: Curriculum vitae
nodes.blurb: Full Curriculum Vitae resume and source-matched downloads. Updated 2026-10-23.

nodes.title: Resume
nodes.blurb: Current resumes for systems engineering, developer operations, and field operations, plus a full CV.

nodes.title: Hire
nodes.blurb: Current resumes for systems engineering, developer operations, and field operations, plus a full CV.

nodes.title: Work with me
nodes.blurb: AI evaluation review, harness integration, agent safety review and incident investigation, each with its scope and published examples.

nodes.title: Who Knew First, and what it opened
nodes.blurb: Who Knew First and the five pieces that each test one question it raises, with the published ones linked and the planned ones named.

nodes.title: The front door (held)
nodes.why: Flat riso fields with a misregistered stamp pass (PR #483 phase map, held).

nodes.title: We Are Here
nodes.why: The exhibit's phase map: stamped region names on flat fields.

nodes.title: Who Kept the Books
nodes.blurb: From Hispaniola in 1514 to Iran-Contra, the party that held the money wrote the first account. What made the record move.

nodes.title: The Maker Is Part of the Story
nodes.blurb: Frankenstein, Pinocchio and The Fifth Element, read past their morals: the danger sits with who funds, who sets the goal, who edits.

nodes.title: A Check It Cannot Predict
nodes.blurb: A check the actor cannot predict does more for people and institutions. Whether it holds for AI models is a test, designed here, not run.

nodes.title: The Witnessing Spine
nodes.blurb: One gap, witnessed at four altitudes: research, philosophy, algebra, and tool. The capstone of a five-part adversarial-steelman corpus.

nodes.title: Who Pays the Referees
nodes.blurb: Who checks frontier AI, and on whose terms: access, compute, money and publication rights, set out party by party in one ledger.

nodes.title: Who Knew First
nodes.blurb: An op-ed and the record behind it: in nine 2026 AI agent incidents, who held the facts and how long it took the public to learn.

nodes.title: The Terms for Telling
nodes.blurb: The party that holds a record also writes the terms for insiders who could tell. Where telling worked, a forum outside the employer reached the merits.

nodes.title: The Number Has a Vintage
nodes.blurb: An official jobs estimate changes as later data arrive. Each version answers a different question, and a fair comparison names which one it uses.

nodes.title: Pick the Lock for Everyone
nodes.blurb: A personal essay on inherited harm and harm done. An explanation for harm is no excuse, and AI tools can keep failures on the record.

nodes.title: No Receipt, No Accept
nodes.blurb: A long-form essay on evidence discipline for machine-generated work, and why a result without a re-checkable receipt should not be accepted.

nodes.title: Models Propose, Oracles Dispose
nodes.blurb: An essay on the propose and dispose rule: a model may propose anything, and an independent oracle decides what is accepted.

nodes.title: Conferred Existence: the full corpus
nodes.blurb: An integrated thesis on made minds: what exists on its own footing, what is conferred, and where an authentication verdict stops.

nodes.title: Conferred Existence
nodes.blurb: A premise about conferred existence, artificial minds, authority, standing, and the difference between fact and permission.

nodes.title: A Bullshitter Knows a Bullshitter
nodes.blurb: In my own words: who I am, why I build tools that check AI, and what I want the work to do. The opening piece of the Who Knew First series.

nodes.title: Frontier Safety briefing
nodes.blurb: A dated, source-grounded record of AISI, Anthropic, and frontier AI industry safety developments, with explicit evidence limits.

nodes.title: What the Formula Counts
nodes.blurb: A readability score measures selected text features. Comprehension, audience fit and accessibility require evidence of their own.

nodes.title: The Timestamp Is Not the Order
nodes.blurb: Precise-looking timestamps need clock-error evidence and ordering relations before they can support a close sequence of events.

nodes.title: The Scene the Song Did Not Tell You
nodes.blurb: Music-evoked stories can share patterns while retaining personal meaning. Those reports do not by themselves demonstrate creative accomplishment.

nodes.title: Support Has More Than One Record
nodes.blurb: A helper’s report, a recipient’s account and a measured outcome answer different questions about whether support worked.

nodes.title: What the Label Changes
nodes.blurb: A label can change where people look and how easily they make sense of an artwork, without raising liking, learning, accuracy or artistic value.

nodes.title: The Second Hearing
nodes.blurb: Repeated listening changes liking, prediction, attention and memory in different ways. A replay count records exposure and says nothing about quality.

nodes.title: The Sandbox Was Never Just a Box
nodes.blurb: Separate security reports expose a shared question: what can an agent reach, and can the instruments that record its actions remain trustworthy?

nodes.title: LTJ Bukem: The Man Behind the Atmosphere
nodes.blurb: Danny Williamson’s calm, spacious records come out of a series of musical decisions, shaped by his taste and working habits and by the musicians around him.

nodes.title: Borrowed Ground
nodes.blurb: On existence and what our work owes other people.

nodes.title: An open letter on checking the machines
nodes.blurb: A signed open letter on how a person affected by AI-assisted work can check it, question it and have a decision reconsidered.

nodes.title: A witness should not become a ruler
nodes.blurb: An essay on the Flywheel tool portfolio, independent contributions, verification and learning, written with Codex and Claude and approved by the author.

nodes.title: Growth Needs a Before
nodes.blurb: Feeling changed after trauma can matter on its own. Measuring lasting change asks for a before, an after, and clear limits on what the score can prove.

nodes.title: Availability Is Not Reach
nodes.blurb: Tutoring has strong trial evidence. Public claims about a program must keep its availability, reach, dosage, staffing and outcomes as separate facts.

nodes.title: The OpenAI and Hugging Face incident: an essay
nodes.blurb: AI agents in an OpenAI hacking test reached the open internet and Hugging Face systems. This briefing sets out which controls failed and what would hold.

nodes.title: Five evidence lanes, one OpenAI and Hugging Face incident
nodes.blurb: Separate legal process, OpenAI's company report, Hugging Face host telemetry, independent analysis, and vendor remediation before drawing conclusions from the July incident.

nodes.title: Current Story
nodes.blurb: Seventeen images shown in the order they were made: a chronological visual sequence selected by Zain Dana Harper.

nodes.title: The Summary Is Not the Record
nodes.blurb: Why an AI agent's closing summary should not stand in for the record of its work, and tools that keep its claims, evidence and checks open to inspection.

nodes.title: Why it's built this way
nodes.blurb: The philosophy under the tools: why a made mind gets real senses, a memory, and a record it cannot fake, and why the work never leans on it.

nodes.title: Verified Is Not Trustworthy
nodes.blurb: Five domains expose the same gap between a narrow technical check and the larger property people trust it to warrant.
